slots.hypothesis: The autocorrelation screen is the one transferable part we have found. On its own it scores negative (-0.18 to -0.81). Used as the x of cs_last_low20, it adds +0.82 to +1.28 (train) and +0.45 to +1.12 (valid) to decay(C). Knocking it out costs +0.34 to +0.77. Seven different inner fields all work, so the content is the outer lag-1 autocorrelation. I read that as a reliability ratio: phi * var(s) / var(x). Names with stale or sparse minute data get excluded, whatever the minute statistic. New periphery: put the screen on y's outside the C family and select instead of only excluding. The y's are S (regbeta and ts_corr forms, window 100/200), a smart-money price ratio Q (top 10% minutes by |r|/sqrt(V), divided by VWAP) and price-volume correlation over the 240 continuous-session minutes. Selection uses cs_first_high40, with 10/20/40% bands. This separates the reliability reading from the reversal-removal reading. Only seed 12 carries the cs_regres(., day_sum(Ret)) step. 13 seeds.

Overnight versus intraday clientele. Overnight O = log(day_first(Open)/cross_delay(day_last(Close),1)) and intraday I = log(day_last(Close)/day_first(Open)); none of the 29 heads sees the overnight segment. Under T+1 and the opening call auction, attention-driven retail demand is priced overnight and continuous trading is priced intraday. For a fixed 20-day move, the share made overnight should be more sentiment-driven and revert more. The 20-day reversal control treats both segments alike. Main line: cs_regres(ts_sum(O,20/60), the explicit close-to-close log return), so the overnight part of plain reversal cannot leak through a control that may be intraday-only. Controls in the seed set: Akbas-style negative-daytime-reversal intensity (continuous, residual and abnormal versus own 120-day mean), the gap-fade tendency ts_corr(O,I), signed auction volume share, and the overnight share of absolute movement. Expected sign is -1. Cheema-Chiah-Man (2022) found the raw tug-of-war intensity has no close-to-close predictive power in China, so the main line does not bet on it. 12 seeds.

The plan:
- **Slot a (E, 13 seeds).** The core is ts_autocorr(day_signed_ratio(Ret, Volume), 60, 1), a subtree of head +1.62 and core card #14. Previous E cores were S and C, so this one has had no E slots. The seeds move the reliability screen onto y's outside the C family and switch from exclusion to selection. The C-free seeds test whether the screen transfers or only removes reversal from C.
- **Slot b (N, 12 seeds).** Overnight versus intraday, built from day_first, day_last and cross_delay, none of which any head uses. Round 1 and 2 N slots already passed audit, so this N is not forced.
- **R (13 variants, 6 groups).**
  - Two near-certain replacements: head +1.49 (decay 30 to 60, already measured at +1.645) and head +0.80 (drop the nested autocorrelation, a known +1.54 form). Both make a stronger near-copy, not a new factor.
  - Seven variants on head +1.89: screen lookback 120/30, lag 2/5, band 10%/5%, and a scale-free version of day_wmean(Volume, Volume).
  - Two on head +1.30: ts_regbeta replaced by ts_corr at windows 200 and 100.
  - Two on the M3 heads: cross_cov to cross_corr on +0.90, and the volatility scale removed from day_wmean(Ret, Ret) on +0.67.
- **Analysis suggestions I left out.** A 40% band (it could replace the top head with a more segment-dependent version), an R on the +0.85 head (yet another C copy), and institutional variables as a second C E slot.

The notebook records my beliefs (C about 80%, the screen real but not itself a source, S at 55% pending the ts_corr test, M2/M3 as traps) and pre-registered predictions. Slot a has about a 55% chance of producing a head, slot b about 30%, and each R variant has a stated pass/fail threshold. It also logs last round's predictions: 6 right, 1 half, 3 wrong, 1 unfalsified.

Four things to watch:
- **Slot a failing on the core.** If the correlation table puts the core at |rho| 0.5 or more with any control, slot a becomes a plain GP. It has not been on a table yet.
- **Book overlap.** On the table, check whether the residual |rho| among the C-family heads clearly exceeds the raw |rho|. That would mean the 0.7 library ban understates how much their books overlap.
- **Slot b's assumption.** The main N seeds are built on the guess that the 20-day reversal control may exclude the overnight gap. I did not inspect the data cube to confirm what Ret includes; the seeds regress on an explicit close-to-close return so they work either way.
- **Citations.** I checked the two new citations (Cheema-Chiah-Man 2022, Barclay-Warner 1993) and the Akbas et al. 2022 details by web search. All are before 2023-08-08.
